title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Nov. 25
gist: A list of seven new technical papers with their research organizations and no analysis. The highlights are a hybrid-bonded 3D NAND analog in-memory compute macro offering 4.8M weights/mm² (IBM Research, Micron, U. of Patras), HBF for GPU systems (Georgia Tech, Nvidia Research, Stanford), defect-aware chiplet matching (ASU, Ampere), backside clock meshes for BSPDN (KAIST), and LLM-agent verification gaps in post-quantum crypto hardware (Lucid Motors, EYL).

insights.claim: IBM Research, Micron Technology and the University of Patras published 3D-NAND-CIM, a hybrid-bonded 3D NAND flash analog in-memory-compute macro that offers 4.8M weights/mm².
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: NAND-based in-memory compute is a possible new AI-inference use for flash; Micron's involvement signals that memory vendors are exploring it.

insights.claim: Georgia Tech, Nvidia Research and Stanford University proposed SlipStream, which enables HBF in GPU systems by mitigating its latency and SRAM overheads.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Nvidia Research working on HBF integration suggests that flash-based high-bandwidth memory tiers are under evaluation for GPU systems, which is relevant to the NAND and HBM supply chains.
insights.quote: Enabling HBF for GPU Systems by Mitigating the Latency and SRAM Overheads

insights.claim: Arizona State University and Ampere Computing presented DT-MATCH, a defect- and topology-aware chiplet matching method for optimizing yield in heterogeneous integration.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Chiplet matching is a yield lever for multi-die products and touches test and packaging economics.
insights.quote: Defect- and Topology-Aware Chiplet Matching for Yield Optimization in Heterogeneous Integration

insights.claim: KAIST studied a clock distribution network with a backside clock mesh in a backside power delivery network (BSPDN) architecture. The site's paper teaser says the approach reduces skew and power.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Moving clock routing to the wafer backside adds to the value of BSPDN at leading-edge nodes.
insights.quote: Backside Clock Mesh Reduces Skew And Power In Backside Power Delivery
insights.locator: Clock Distribution Network with Backside Clock Mesh

insights.claim: Lucid Motors and EYL Inc. measured what tests and reviews miss when LLM agents generate post-quantum cryptographic hardware, going from FIPS specifications to FPGA.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Verification gaps in LLM-generated security hardware are a risk flag for AI-driven chip design flows and a demand signal for stronger verification.
insights.quote: Measuring What Tests and Reviews Miss in Post-Quantum Cryptographic Hardware
insights.locator: From FIPS to FPGA with LLM Agents

insights.claim: Singapore University of Technology and Design, A*STAR and the National University of Singapore proposed self-supervised, attention-based virtual metrology to predict CMP material removal rate (MRR).
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
entities: Singapore University of Technology and Design
insights.so_what: ML-based virtual metrology can cut physical measurement steps in CMP, which is relevant to process-control spending.

insights.claim: AMO GmbH and RWTH Aachen University studied how electron-beam writing-field stitching affects optical losses in silicon-on-insulator waveguides. The site teaser says stitching errors increase loss.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: E-beam stitching artifacts are a loss source in SOI photonics prototyping, a niche but real yield and performance factor.
insights.quote: E-Beam Stitching Errors Increase Loss In SOI Waveguides
insights.locator: The Impact of Writing Field Stitching
